summary: A first-person narrator meets with a lawyer who agrees to represent them, and they discuss a case involving the narrator's brother Danny, an informant named Zip, and an FBI meeting set for that morning. The lawyer explains that entrapment defenses depend on inducement and predisposition, and the two discuss news coverage of the case in the Star Tribune and Pioneer Press. The excerpt also includes an unrelated sentence about Megan seeing the 'Garden of Earthly Delights' painting in 2013.
one_line: A narrator retains a lawyer over a terrorism-related case involving their brother Danny and an informant named Zip, weighing entrapment and media attention.
key_facts: The narrator asks the lawyer to represent them, and she agrees to become their attorney.
The narrator says they have no money to pay the lawyer.
The meeting with FBI agents is set for the morning following the conversation.
The lawyer says the two key issues in cases like this are inducement and predisposition.
The lawyer explains that if the state can show Wilson was ready and eager to participate in a terrorist act, the defense is in trouble.
The narrator's brother is named Danny, and the informant is named Zip.
The narrator told the lawyer about Simon and Danny and the meeting with FBI agents.
Danny talked about possible targets, but when Simon pushed him, the note indicates the narrator's account was cut off.
The Star Tribune front page headline reads 'Local Case Gets the Hollywood Treatment.'
The Pioneer Press ran an article headlined 'Lilmmaker Locuses Her Lens on Minneapolis' down the right side of its front page.
The lawyer suggests the media attention may help the case.
In 2013, Megan waited in line for hours and then saw the original 'Garden of Earthly Delights' painting up close.
The narrator says they did not tell the lawyer what happened after they left the punk house.
The lawyer jokes that the narrator can say 'will you represent me as my attorney?' to hire her.
